conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim that flu vaccination causes Alzheimer's disease is false and unsupported by scientific evidence, citing research showing either no causal link or a reduced risk. Therefore, it clearly rejects the claim.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
Your skepticism is well-founded — the claim that flu vaccination *causes* Alzheimer's disease is false and unsupported by scientific evidence.

**Origin of the myth:** The claim traces back to Hugh Fudenberg, a discredited immunologist whose license was revoked; he asserted that repeated flu vaccination increases Alzheimer's risk tenfold due to mercury/aluminum content, but never published peer-reviewed data supporting this. Fact-checking outlets have labeled the claim "mostly false" (https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/flu-shot-avoidance/).

**What actual research shows:** Multiple peer-reviewed cohort studies show the opposite association — flu vaccination is linked to *reduced* Alzheimer's/dementia risk, not increased risk:

- A large retrospective cohort study found individuals vaccinated against flu were 40% less likely to develop Alzheimer's disease (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9484126/).
- A 2026 study found high-dose flu vaccines were associated with significantly lower Alzheimer's risk than standard-dose vaccines in adults 65+, with stronger protection in women (https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000214782).
- A broader analysis found multiple adult vaccines (flu, shingles, pneumococcal, Tdap) were associated with lower dementia risk overall (https://academic.oup.com/ageing/article/54/11/afaf331/8339764).
- The Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation explicitly reviewed this myth and concluded there is "no peer-reviewed scientific evidence" supporting a causal link, and evidence instead points to a protective association (https://www.alzdiscovery.org/cognitive-vitality/blog/is-there-a-link-between-alzheimers-disease-and-the-flu-shot).

**Conclusion:** The causal claim is false; it originated from an unsubstantiated source, and current evidence suggests flu vaccination may lower dementia/Alzheimer's risk, though researchers note more work is needed to confirm mechanisms and causality.
